item.title: Interesting Stuff - Week 41, 2026
item.description:
This week the theme is small, sharp and scheduled: tiny models that decide, harnesses that learn, and agents that quietly do their job while you sleep. Six posts cover System 1 “decider” models with a working router, Microsoft’s lightweight agentic RL framework, Claude Code mods, Pinterest’s LLM-powered user journeys, an AI-assisted learning framework, and Anthropic’s recipe for agent automations that don’t fail silently.

If last week was about who holds the steering wheel, this week is about what happens when you let go of it, safely. Grab a coffee, and let’s dive in.

item.title: Interesting Stuff - Week 40, 2026
item.description:
Three posts this week, and the common thread is control: who gets to steer the model, the agent, and the tool. One model refuses to write a single word and only hands you code-typed decisions, Asana shows what it takes to treat AI agents like coachable colleagues, and Anthropic hands you the keys to Claude Code itself.

Jev swaps chatty paragraphs for calibrated probabilities, Asana’s Arnab Bose explains how agents get roles, memory and an audit trail, and Claude Code mods let you rewrite the product with a few lines of TypeScript. Grab a coffee, and let’s dive in.
